# @microsoft/managed-apps-common

Shared types, utilities, and services used across the Microsoft managed apps packages — the channel/communication protocol, the transport-agnostic data client, HTTP client, errors, telemetry, and common domain types (no DOM dependency). Internal package published for reuse within the stack.

The `gateway` entry point includes experimental local-development snapshot,
data-only initialization and backend result schemas, plus the shared
`interpretInitDevSessionResponse` classifier. The `communication` entry point
declares the pre-identity loader bootstrap and `Methods.Dev` contracts; importing
them does not register handlers or enable local-dev behavior. See
[phase-0 contracts](../../docs/architecture/microsoft-apps/local-dev-contracts.md).

The Zod configuration contract in `src/config` is the source of truth for the app config JSON
Schemas. `scripts/generate-json-schema.ts` renders it into `dist/ms.config.schema.json` (exported
as `@microsoft/managed-apps-common/config/ms.config.schema.json`) during the build, and into
`dist/stage-overlay.schema.json` for the deployment overlay.

`data.schemaPath` is the canonical schema source setting; `db.schemaPath` remains a legacy
alias. Runtime `ConfigSchemaV0` validation rejects malformed aliases and requires exact,
unnormalized path-string equality when both are present. The generated JSON Schema describes
both fields and marks `db` as deprecated; cross-field equality is enforced at runtime.
Neither alias is stage-overridable, and effective configs preserve the fields as authored.
The config entry point exports `DataConfig` and its deprecated compatibility alias `DbConfig`.

Both config aliases accept optional boolean `enabled`. Explicit values on both aliases must agree;
if only one supplies a value, pack uses it. Pack copies that boolean to optional
`PackManifest.dataEnabled`, preserving `false` and omitting the field when unset. The flag does not
control schema validation or packaging, and `schemaPath` remains required.

Those schemas are published in the public
[`microsoft/Managed-Apps`](https://github.com/microsoft/Managed-Apps) repo under `schemas/`, which
is what the `$schema` pointer in a generated `ms.config.json` / `ms.<deployment>.config.json`
targets (`AppConfigSchemaUrl`, `StageOverlaySchemaUrl`). Regenerate them there rather than editing
by hand:

```bash
bun scripts/generate-json-schema.ts <path-to-Managed-Apps>/schemas
```
